input_format: raw: one control byte selecting UDP/TCP and an optional waiting callback, followed by one DNS wire-format response
configuration_profile: direct asynchronous resolver response parser with a fuzz-only pending-query setup hook
allocator_mode: nginx resolver allocator plus a per-input nginx pool
justification: DNS responses are untrusted network input and were explicitly left as a follow-up outside the original six scopes.
state: A fresh resolver and matching pending A, AAAA, SRV, or IPv4 PTR query are created per input; mode bit 1 optionally attaches a self-freeing no-op waiter to exercise asynchronous completion, no sockets are opened and no state crosses inputs.
known_limitations: The target parses one complete UDP or TCP DNS message, not TCP length framing or socket events.
Truncated UDP responses are parsed without installing a pending node so the harness never initiates TCP fallback.
IPv6 PTR pending-query setup is not modeled; its question parser remains reachable but a matching addr6 node is not installed.
The setup hook is applied only to the isolated instrumented build copy.

scopes.contract: Validates and dispatches one DNS response or rejects malformed header/question data.
scopes.preconditions: Initialized resolver trees/queues/log and a pending query whose ID, name and type match an uncompressed single-question response.

scopes.contract: Correlates and parses A/AAAA/CNAME answers, updates the address cache and completes waiters.
scopes.preconditions: A matching pending name node exists.

scopes.contract: Parses SRV/CNAME answers and stores sorted service records.
scopes.preconditions: A matching pending SRV node exists; success callbacks that would start child DNS queries are not installed.

scopes.contract: Parses reverse lookup answers, caches the name and completes waiters.
scopes.preconditions: A matching pending IPv4 address node exists.

scopes.contract: Decodes DNS labels and compression pointers with bounds and loop checks.
scopes.preconditions: The source starts within a padded DNS packet and last marks its logical end.
